findings.what: Calcified Tissue International published a systematic review (Falvino and colleagues) of 26 animal studies of drugs acting on aged cells in osteoarthritis, osteoporosis and muscle loss; it finds protective effects in mice and says the studies differ too much to draw firm conclusions. Abstract read on Europe PMC.

records.found: Two peer-reviewed mouse reports dated in the window say that clearing aged cells lengthened life: a Nature Aging paper of 2026-11-06 on vanadyl sulfate, a dietary supplement, in male mice, and an Advanced Science paper of 2026-10-28 on a vaccine against aged cells. Both are at the animal rung this entry already holds, and neither is a trial in people, so the test for the next stage is not met. No human trial with a lifespan or healthy-years measure was registered or reported in the window.

findings.what: Nature Aging published a paper (Wu and colleagues; last author Chen) reporting that vanadyl sulfate, a mineral sold as a dietary supplement, kills aged cells and, given by mouth, lengthened the lives of male mice. Read as the abstract on Europe PMC and the Crossref record; the journal page asked for a sign-in.

Advanced Science published a paper from the First Hospital of Jilin University (Song and colleagues) reporting that a vaccine aimed at the surface protein GPNMB on aged cells cleared aged fat cells in several mouse models and lengthened the mice's lives. Abstract read on Europe PMC.

records.found: On 2026-11-05 the Steadman Philippon Research Institute first posted a registry entry (NCT07918261) for an 82-person fisetin trial it finished on 2024-01-30, whose main measure is the change in aged immune cells in the blood; no results are posted, so it does not add to or count against the record yet. No approval and no new peer-reviewed human measurement was dated in the window. Mayo Clinic's fisetin trial in people in hospital with COVID-19 (NCT04476953) was updated on 2026-11-03 and still has no results.

findings.what: The Steadman Philippon Research Institute first posted a registry entry (NCT07918261) for a trial it finished on 2024-01-30: 82 people, randomised but open-label, given the plant compound fisetin; the main measure is the change in aged immune cells in the blood after 45 days. No results are posted.

Mayo Clinic's placebo-controlled fisetin trial in adults in hospital with COVID-19 (NCT04476953, 80 people) had its registry entry updated; it is listed as active, not recruiting, with completion now estimated for March 2027 and no results posted.
A letter in the Journal of Biochemical and Molecular Toxicology (Raajasekar) is titled 'Clinical Viability of Fisetin Limited by High Risk of Drug-Drug Interactions'. Only the title was seen.

records.found: Still animals only: no trial of such cells in people was registered or updated in the window. Cell Stem Cell published on 2026-10-29 a mouse study in which engineered T cells aimed at uPAR, the same surface protein as this entry's record, improved muscle in a model of Duchenne muscular dystrophy, and Advanced Science published on 2026-10-28 a mouse study of a vaccine against the GPNMB protein named in the notes. A press release of 2026-11-05 about a review of the field says the work has not reached people or any regulator.

findings.what: Cell Stem Cell published a mouse study (Afzal and colleagues; last author Diao) in which T cells engineered to recognise uPAR removed harmful cell groups in the muscle of mice with a form of Duchenne muscular dystrophy and improved muscle and breathing function. It is a different disease from ageing and the abstract does not describe the target cells as aged cells. Abstract read on Europe PMC; Crossref gives the month only.

Advanced Science published a paper from the First Hospital of Jilin University (Song and colleagues) reporting that a vaccine aimed at the surface protein GPNMB on aged cells cleared aged fat cells in several mouse models and lengthened the mice's lives. Abstract read on Europe PMC.

A press release on EurekAlert describes a review in the journal Research (Shao and colleagues, Zhejiang University School of Medicine) of engineered T cells against aged cells; it says the work is in animals and 'not been approved by any regulatory authority', and announces no trial. Crossref dates the review itself to 2026-06-12, before the window.

unmatched.what: A planned trial of whether lung rehabilitation and metformin act against aged cells in people with flare-ups of chronic lung disease (NCT07275359) had its registry entry updated; it is not yet recruiting and is due to start in February 2027. Seen in the registry listing only.
unmatched.why_it_matters: A coming human trial that measures aged cells, on the same branch as these records but with a drug not built to kill them.
